BENGALURU RURAL DISTRICT, AS AGAINST THE PRESENT PETITIONER (ACCUSED NO.1) AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Petitioner-accused No.1 is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 306 of IPC.

2. The 2nd respondent lodged the FIR stating that accused No.1 is the legally wedded wife of her deceased son and accused No.1 had developed illicit intimacy with one Shekar and she was caught red handed and in this regard Panchayats were convened and accused No.1 was advised to mend her ways.
However, accused No.1 did not mend her ways and left the matrimonial home and was residing in her parental home.

Thereafter, the accused No.1 was calling the deceased and threatening him that she would register two more cases against them in addition to the case already registered in Crime No.59/2021 for the offence 498A and section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. On 17.4.2021, the accused herein along with accused No. 2 and 3 came to the house of the deceased and picked up the quarrel and accused No.1 took all clothes belonging to her and threatened the deceased that she would file cases against him and his family members and send them to Jail.
On 19.04.2021, at about 8.00 pm the 2nd respondent was informed that her son had NC: 2024:KHC:21105 committed suicide by hanging.
The Registration of FIR is impugned in this petition.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

5. The only allegation against the petitioner-accused No.1, she threatened the deceased that she would file multiple cases, in addition to the complaint filed in Crime No.59/2021 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

Further, on Smt. Suvarna vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160402734/

6. The Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions has held that, to constitute an offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC, the following essential elements must be satisfied:
i) There must be an intention on the part of the accused to aid or instigate or abet the deceased to commit suicide.
ii) There must be a suicidal death and abetment thereof.
iii) There must a continuous harassment meted out by the accused before the death.
NC: 2024:KHC:21105 iv) Such irritation or annoying must be proximate to the time of occurrence of death.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Geo Varghese -vs- State of Rajasthan and another (2021 SCC OnLine SC 873) at para-23 has held as follows:
"23.

entities.text: Geo Varghese -vs- State of Rajasthan and another (2021 SCC OnLine SC 873)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: What is required to constitute an alleged abetment of suicide under Section 306 IPC is there must be an allegation of either direct or indirect act of incitement to the commission of offence of suicide and mere allegations of harassment of the deceased by another person would not be sufficient in itself, unless, there are allegations of such actions on the part of the accused which compelled the commission of suicide.

Further if the person committing suicide is hypersensitive and the allegations attributed to the accused is otherwise not ordinarily expected to induce a similarly situated persons to take the extreme step of committing suicide, it would be unsafe to hold the accused guilty of abetment of suicide.

Thus, what is required is an examination of every case on its own facts and circumstances and keeping in consideration the surrounding circumstances as well, which may have bearing on the alleged action of the accused and the psyche of the deceased."
8.
In the instant case, the essential elements so as to constitute the commission of an offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC against the Petitioner-accused No.1 are conspicuously absent.
Therefore, the continuation of the investigation against the petitioner-accused No.1 will be an abuse of process of law.
